_meta.role: Embedded Software Engineer, Implant Embedded Systems

summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT) with hands on bare metal firmware experience on STM32 Cortex M4, including register level GPIO, timer, ADC, and I2C programming under FreeRTOS. Designed and fabricated custom PCBs in EAGLE with interrupt driven UART and I2C sensor integration, and built firmware for real time sensor sampling under deterministic timing constraints. Background in digital signal processing and electrical engineering fundamentals from a B.E. in Electronics and Telecommunication grounds this firmware work in the underlying hardware.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth to translate 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Programmed peripherals directly in bare-metal C (GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1) on an STM32 Cortex-M4; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at a deterministic 1 Hz update rate, verified in Proteus.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver for real-time sensor communication.
Built temperature-monitoring firmware in embedded C with timer-synchronized sensing and real-time display at the register level.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination on an STM32 target; integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing and OLED distance visualization.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART command handling and user override.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors (camera range-gate + gripper-triggered close at 25 mm) for contact-aware grasping via a TCA9548A I2C multiplexer.
Resolved 11 integration failures across the embedded control stack (servo brown-out, stale-frame capture) to reach 100% pick reliability over 10 trials.

awards: 1st Prize, CanSat Workshop — Arduino Nano atmospheric data collection during free fall (2023)
Ranked 10th, Robocon — National-level robotics competition among 45 universities (2022)
